html:
The capture of Kaifeng, capital of the Northern Song dynasty, by the Jurchen Jin dynasty in 1126 and 1127. The Chinese remember it as the Jingkang incident, after the year name of the time.

The Song had allied with the Jurchens to destroy the Liao state in the north. The Jurchens then turned on their weak ally. Their armies besieged Kaifeng, took huge payments, came back and stormed it. They carried off the retired emperor Huizong, the reigning emperor Qinzong, thousands of members of the court and the palace treasures to the far north, where both emperors died in captivity.

A brother of Qinzong escaped and refounded the dynasty in the south, with its capital at Hangzhou, as the Southern Song. North China stayed under Jin rule for a century, until the Mongols took it. Song general Yue Fei, who fought to win the north back, became a national hero.
sum: The capture of Kaifeng, capital of the Northern Song dynasty, by the Jurchen Jin dynasty in 1126 and 1127. The Chinese remember it as the Jingkang incident, after the year name of the time.
